A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TAPIP3D work, with matching authors, architecture and main experiments. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable across both complete PDFs. v1 ends with references; v2 includes Appendices A–F.

before.justification: Section 4 and Tables 1–5 report original tracking evaluations and ablations on real and synthetic datasets.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical evaluations and adds neighborhood-size results, runtime measurements and qualitative stereo-video examples.

M1.justification: The stated trajectory-update token drops the confidence input c between v1 Equation 3 and v2 Equation 2. The feature clouds, k-NN neighborhoods, bidirectional attention and iterative refinement remain matched. Renaming Local Pair Attention to N2N and expanding its implementation description do not establish further architectural changes.

E1.justification: Appendix C and Figure 5 add qualitative evaluation on in-the-wild VR180 stereo videos using FoundationStereo-derived depth. Kubric training and the TAPVid-3D, DexYCB-Pt, LSFOdyssey and Dynamic Replica benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain CoTracker3 plus depth, SpatialTracker and DELTA in the corresponding comparisons. The attention-ablation variants match across renamed rows. FoundationStereo supplies depth rather than serving as a competing tracker, and the runtime comparison retains SpatialTracker.

E3.justification: The added analyses introduce inference-time testing at K = 16, 24, 32 and 48 with a model trained at K = 32, and a runtime protocol using 32 frames, 1,024 queries, BF16 and one L40S GPU. These extend the evaluation design; the newly documented settings for retained benchmarks do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 5b extends the attention ablation to DexYCB-Pt, and Appendix D adds neighborhood-size sensitivity analysis. Figures 4–5 add a qualitative baseline-drift comparison and stereo examples. The original ablations remain. The second dataset in the new sensitivity study is inconsistently identified as DexYCB in the prose and Dynamic Replica in Table 7.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The additional results continue single-value reporting without a stated uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the existing LSFOdyssey entries in Table 5 are numerically unchanged. New results include DexYCB attention-ablation AJ3D scores of 26.3 without N2N and 29.8 with it, neighborhood-size results and qualitative examples. Table 8 reports 11.3 FPS versus SpatialTracker's 14.6; v1 only stated an approximately 1.5-fold slowdown under unspecified conditions, so a cross-version speedup is not established.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds an analytical computational-cost expression for N2N attention, O(TNK^2D + TNKD^2), with its variables defined. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs, and the main depth-weighted tracking and visibility loss remains matched.

C1.justification: The introduction changes the claim that TAPIP3D is the only method capable of world-centric 3D tracking to the weaker claim that it is a pioneering method. The central contributions and claims about camera stabilization and performance with accurate depth remain.

C2.justification: v2 retains the depth-quality limitation but adds completion, noise filtering and stereo depth as possible mitigations. Appendix D identifies N2N attention as a computational bottleneck and motivates K = 32 as an accuracy–efficiency compromise. The principal interpretations of the original benchmark results remain.

D1.justification: Appendices A–C substantially expand reproducibility information: loss weights and discounting, gradient clipping, memory-saving backpropagation, reverse-time inference, a 16-by-16 support-query grid, ground-truth-dependent evaluation normalization and stereo preprocessing. v2 also reports BF16 usage, training time and VRAM consumption. These are chiefly new disclosures. Table 6 lists batch size 8 while the main text retains 1, without explaining the aggregation convention.

R1.justification: v2 adds Stereo4D and FoundationStereo references supporting the stereo application and removes Track2Act, RoboTAP and General Flow citations accompanying the earlier robotics motivation. It also softens the exclusive novelty claim. The main related-work comparisons remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively recast around an explicit research question. The method overview, coordinate-system discussion, CoTracker preliminaries and attention explanation are substantially rewritten, with clearer stepwise descriptions of support and context tokens. Terminology is standardized around feature clouds and N2N, and a structured supplement is added.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, substantially repositioning and resizing existing displays. Architecture and attention diagrams receive revised labels and captions. v2 adds Figures 4–5 and Tables 6–8 and expands Table 5b with DexYCB-Pt columns.

improvement.justification: The rewritten method and Appendices A–B improve clarity and reproducibility, while the sensitivity study and qualitative comparisons add useful supporting evidence. The main benchmark results remain unchanged. These gains are moderated by reporting inconsistencies, particularly Appendix D naming DexYCB where Table 7 labels Dynamic Replica, and the main text reporting 10 FPS versus 11.3 FPS in Table 8.
